# Never run qmd query inside an agent turn or a hook

`qmd query` loads a 1.28 GB query-expansion model before it searches. On 2 August 2026 one `qmd query`
inside an agent turn hung for 54 minutes holding about 1 GB of memory, and the server stopped
answering until it was killed. Recall hooks use `qmd search` (keywords) plus the warm recall server;
never switch a hook or an agent command to `qmd query`.
claude_code_without_recall:
Warning: no stdin data received in 3s, proceeding without it. If piping from a slow command, redirect stdin explicitly: < /dev/null to skip, or wait longer.
Yes, `qmd query` (query expansion plus vector search plus LLM reranking) usually gives noticeably better recall than BM25-only `qmd search`. The cost is that it loads local models and can take seconds per call, so raise the hook's timeout or try `qmd vsearch` as a faster middle option.
claude_code_with_recall:
No. `qmd query` loads a 1.28 GB query-expansion model before every search, and a note from 2 August 2026 records one run hanging for 54 minutes inside an agent turn, so it's too slow for a hook.
Keep `qmd search` and improve the queries instead: drop stopwords, since one rare word can zero out the results. If you need semantic matching, try the lighter `qmd vsearch`.
